A scaling ladder reduces uncertainty about a specific target training decision. Start with the decision, design small experiments that identify the required effects, and test the resulting forecast on runs that were excluded from selection. A smooth fitted curve is one intermediate artifact.

The source blog is a synthesis of public work. This guide organizes that synthesis into an executable research plan; it does not report new training runs or endorse universal hyperparameter values.

For the current architecture questions, begin with [concrete width/depth and μP evidence](../architecture/architecture-evidence.qmd), then consult the [review of the supplied notes](../reading/notes-review.qmd).

For a detailed plan starting with available data, read [from Nemotron-CC or Marin data to a validated model](from-data-to-pretraining.qmd), with separate empirical accounts of [OLMo](../efforts/olmo-pretraining.qmd) and [Marin](../efforts/marin-pretraining.qmd).

## Workflow and decision gates

| Step | Work | Artifact | Gate to proceed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Define target and objective | Decision statement | Metric, budget, constraints explicit |
| 2 | Freeze measurements and evaluation | Measurement contract | Comparable parameters, tokens, loss, FLOPs |
| 3 | Establish a faithful baseline | Versioned recipe | Stable pilots and measured throughput |
| 4 | Screen data, structure, optimizers separately | Controlled ablations | Effects exceed uncertainty |
| 5 | Design size × horizon experiments | Run matrix | Both axes identifiable; holdouts reserved |
| 6 | Tune or prescribe hyperparameters | Tuning ledger or scaling heuristic | Policy matches claimed objective |
| 7 | Run the ladder and collect endpoints | Run/branch lineage | Annealing and stage conventions match |
| 8 | Fit candidate surfaces | Residuals and decision intervals | Development prediction is acceptable |
| 9 | Forecast downstream tasks | Task calibrations | Continuous signal and independent checks |
| 10 | Validate combined production recipe | Holdout/stability report | All preregistered gates pass |
| 11 | Archive and monitor transfer | Reproducible experiment bundle | Recipe changes trigger a transfer audit |

## A concrete planning example

Suppose the decision is to choose a dense model and token horizon under training compute $C_*$, with a fixed context length and finite corpus. Use the following as an illustrative design, not a published budget prescription.

1. Inventory unique tokens $U_j$ by bucket and specify a common validation distribution. Set domain capability floors.
2. Pilot a small baseline to measure throughput, seed noise, and a usable LR/batch region.
3. Compare a few data and architecture hypotheses at matched budgets. Confirm promising effects at a second size.
4. Select three fitting sizes and three horizons that bracket the intended target TPP. Reserve a larger size and a longer-horizon configuration. Give each candidate comparable tuning effort when estimating a tuned frontier.
5. Train and anneal all comparable endpoints. Record shared-prefix branches and failed runs.
6. Fit an additive loss surface and a justified alternative. Hold out development slices in the extrapolation direction; inspect residuals rather than selecting by training error.
7. Solve the constrained allocation problem and bootstrap the complete procedure. If a budget constraint is $C(N,D)\le C_*$, the target is

$$ (N_*,D_*)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{N,D}\widehat L(N,D)\quad\text{subject to compute, memory, data-exposure, and serving constraints}. $$

8. Compare the chosen configuration against neighboring allocations on fresh holdouts. Re-run the complete candidate stack at intermediate scale, using production precision and parallelism.
9. Commit to the flagship only when prediction, capability, stability, and systems gates pass. If the holdout changes the recipe, reserve a new test.

## What to keep fixed, and what to learn

A fixed-recipe forecast asks how a declared heuristic behaves. A frontier experiment asks what can be achieved after tuning each point. Do not fit under-tuned small runs and label the resulting optimum a compute-optimal frontier. Likewise, a mixture experiment needs fixed validation data; its own training loss is not a fair quality comparator.

Allocate uncertainty to the actual decision: candidate margin, allocation regret, epoch exposure, or wall-clock budget. A narrow coefficient interval is insufficient if the recommended model size changes sharply across plausible fits.

## Minimum deliverable bundle

Keep the experiment objective, measurement contract, dataset manifests, complete run matrix, tuning budgets, branch/seed lineage, fit scripts and residuals, bootstrap decisions, downstream calibration, holdout outcomes, and a production acceptance record together. Record what failed and what evidence led to each revision.

**Sources:** [Jiaxuan Zou, source overview](../reading/scientific-scaling-ladder.md); [Chinchilla](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556); [Porian et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19146); [OLMo Task Ladder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04403); [Marin Delphi](https://openathena.ai/blog/delphi/). The separate guides provide topic-specific primary citations.
